memory_lessons.applicability: CTA source-tile size should be compared under the official protocol; aggregate measurements do not identify per-size effects.
memory_lessons.claim: Both the 128- and 256-thread shared-tile candidates passed correctness. Their measured means were 0.00096318 s and 0.00099616 s respectively, versus the 0.00184441 s baseline. These results support testing tile sizes but do not establish a universal best size.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure a 512-thread source tile to test whether fewer tile iterations and barriers offset its larger CTA and shared-memory footprint.

proposal.hypothesis: The measured 128-thread tile (0.00096318 s) was faster than the 256-thread tile (0.00099616 s), but the difference does not show whether a larger tile can amortize tile-loop and barrier overhead. Test a 512-thread CTA staging 512 sources (14,336 shared-memory bytes), retaining one target per thread and source order; the larger CTA and shared-memory footprint could also reduce occupancy, so no speedup is assumed.

retained: Set block and items_per_block to 512, with a 14,336-byte shared-memory allocation for 512 Particle records.
Stage source particles in CTA-sized tiles and reuse each tile across the block's active targets, keeping exactly one target per thread and ascending source interaction order.
Keep all threads participating in both barriers, including threads without valid output targets; handle partial source tiles and guard target reads and output writes.
